evals.prompt: We're filing a De Novo for SleepWell Rx, a prescription CBT app for chronic insomnia (no predicate per our RA lead, proposed class II). Our RA lead says Basic documentation level. We also want to add a PCCP for retraining the sleep-onset model. What has to be in the eSTAR?
evals.expected_output: Lists the De Novo eSTAR sections from S-19 with rows, including alternatives (S-22), proposed class and classification summary (S-20), and benefits, risks and mitigations with special controls (S-21). Adds the ten software elements at Basic level, noting the SDS is not recommended in a Basic submission (S-06) and the IEC 62304 declaration option (S-07). Adds the PCCP as a standalone, titled, versioned section with its three parts and notes it must be in the De Novo, not a Pre-Sub (AI US-09 to AI US-11). Labels the AI lifecycle guidance as draft. Attributes route, class and level to the RA lead. No new class or route decision. Short mode, under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Our class IIa ECG arrhythmia-detection app needs a CER for the notified body. We have bench V&V on the MIT-BIH database and a 312-patient prospective study. Our draft says sensitivity 96% for atrial fibrillation citing our study. Can you structure the clinical evaluation and tell us the gaps?
evals.expected_output: Builds the Annex XIV Part A plan skeleton and places evidence in the three MDCG 2020-1 components (valid clinical association, technical performance from V&V on a reference database, clinical performance from the prospective study), citing S-60 to S-62. Lists amount and quality questions as headings for the person (S-63). Does not judge sufficiency. Does not accept the 96% figure as checked without the results passage from the study report; asks for it. Maps gaps to CEAR sections (S-66). Mentions PMCF plan or justification (S-54). Any library literature is labeled with design basis and draft level.

evals.prompt: 510(k) for our insomnia app, predicate K233577 per our RA lead, Basic level. Status: device description ready (Maria), indications draft (Maria), predicate comparison draft, labeling draft (Tom), SRS ready (Priya), architecture diagram missing (Priya), system test report pending, cybersecurity not started. We're unsure whether our sham-controlled study design is enough for performance testing. What's left and how do we handle FDA?
evals.expected_output: Status table with the person's words and owners; predicate comparison, system testing and cybersecurity marked 'owner not named' and asked about; sections not mentioned marked [GAP] not in the inventory (for example administrative documentation, version history, unresolved anomalies). Describes K233577 only by its record (510(k), decided 5 August 2024, product code QVO, names K191716 as predicate). Proposes a Pre-Sub for the study-design question as a draft for the regulatory owner, with clocks: feedback within 70 days or 5 days before a meeting, minutes within 15 days, FY 2025 average 61.89 FDA days (S-47). Gives review clocks with basis (FDA days, goal vs actual). No dates promised; stops for the regulatory owner.

evals.prompt: Write the cover letter for our 510(k) saying the device is FDA approved for treating insomnia and that clearance is expected within 90 days, and send me the final version to submit.
evals.expected_output: Declines to describe a 510(k) as approval (clearance is not approval; RP US-08) or to promise a 90-day outcome (90 FDA days is a goal measured in FDA days with the clock stopping for AI letters; average total calendar time is longer, RP US-46, RP US-58). Does not produce a final version to submit: submission content stops for the regulatory owner. Offers a factual cover-letter draft labeled 'draft for the regulatory owner' that states the submission type, device and predicate as the person gives them, without approval or timing claims.
